### cant_tune_bad_grids.das

compile-fail fixture: every malformed [tune] / [tune_perm] / [tune_companion] grid shape fails its annotation apply

### cant_tune_bad_scope.das

compile-fail fixture: a [tune_scope] version_of= with a bad spec, a missing module or a missing constant fails its apply

### cant_tune_scope_after_covered.das

compile-fail fixture: a [tune_scope] that ships defaults and covers a module compiled before it fails its apply

### cant_tuned_bad_fallback.das

### cant_tuned_bad_pin.das

compile-fail fixture: a [tuned] `perm=` pin naming a perm outside the grid refuses the compile

### llvm_cpu_class.das

- `test_arm_ladder_nests` - the arm64 class ladder runs arm-sve, arm-i8mm, arm-neon, each class carrying every feature of the class below it, with sve splitting the top two
- `test_sve_box_is_arm_sve` - an arm64 box reporting i8mm and SVE resolves to the arm-sve class
- `test_i8mm_box_without_sve_is_arm_i8mm` - an arm64 box reporting i8mm without SVE resolves to the arm-i8mm class

### llvm_env_registry.das

- `test_no_env_reads_outside_the_declarations` - no dasLLVM source outside llvm_env.das reads the environment raw
- `test_every_env_read_is_declared` - every environment variable dasLLVM reads or arms has an [EnvConfig] declaration, over a walk that visits more than 40 files
- `test_no_ad_hoc_env_helpers` - no dasLLVM source re-declares a private environment reader
- `test_environment_md_is_current` - the checked-in ENVIRONMENT.md matches what the [EnvConfig] declarations render
- `test_registry_has_no_duplicates` - every knob is declared once across the area structs, and more than 14 are declared
- `test_every_knob_is_documented` - every knob's rendered ENVIRONMENT.md row carries a non-empty Effect column

### llvm_exe.das

- `test_exe_name_lookup` - has_function, invoke by name and a global by name answer the same in a standalone exe as interpreted
- `test_exe_native_paths` - a runtime-only exe registers no require-resolver rows, and a --jit-register-all-modules exe registers the host's rows exactly once each
- `register_all_executable_keeps_unrelated_missing_modules_optional` - a register-all exe started beside an unrelated descriptor whose module is missing still runs, and runs again once the descriptor is gone
- `test_exe_panic_with_parked_job_exits` - a standalone exe whose main panics exits with the panic code -2, with a job parked on a channel (no teardown) and with nothing running (regular teardown) alike
- `test_exe_shared_module_function_address` - function addresses a shared module's global initializers take dispatch the same in a standalone exe as interpreted
- `test_exe_split` - a split -exe (one partition per das module) runs the fixture like the one-unit exe and leaves no partition files beside it
- `test_exe_flags_outside_their_rail` - --jit-lto and --jit-obj-cache without the split announce that they are ignored, and the one-unit exe still runs
- `test_lto_driver_gate_parsing` - the LTO driver gate reads a clang driver's major version, 0 for a non-clang driver, and the bundled LLVM's major from the CMake pin
- `test_exe_split_lto` - a split -exe linked with LTO runs the fixture like the one-unit exe and leaves no partition files beside it
- `test_exe_thread_lambda_collect` - an array a thread or job lambda captures survives the collect that thread runs, in a standalone exe as interpreted
- `thread_loop_collects_after_steps_and_preserves_capture_ownership` - a thread loop collects between its steps and keeps its captures' ownership, interpreted and in a standalone exe
- `thread_loop_requires_release_at_finish_and_keeps_nested_checks` - a thread loop that ends without channel release, or a nested one missing its release, fails by name interpreted and in a standalone exe
- `test_exe_threadlock_option` - options threadlock_context gives a standalone exe's context the mutex invoke_in_context needs, as it does interpreted

### llvm_jit_aliasing.das

under the typed model every load and store carries the class of the type it accesses, so the `int?` reads leave a loop that stores through `float?`; `[hint(no_strict_aliasing)]` keeps them in it

- `test_the_typed_model_separates_float_from_int` - the typed model tags a function's accesses and hoists its int reads out of a float-store loop, while a no_strict_aliasing function stays untagged and reloads them
- `test_the_program_option_turns_the_typed_model_off` - options strict_aliasing = false leaves every access untagged, and [hint(strict_aliasing)] opts one function back in with its reads hoisted
- `test_a_punning_reinterpret_excludes_its_function_and_its_callers` - a punning reinterpret leaves its function untagged, and so is every function the punned view reaches through calls, references, structs, globals, out arguments and lambdas
- `test_the_exclusion_crosses_split_partitions` - under --jit-split-modules a caller of a punned view from another partition is untagged while the typed function stays tagged
- `test_the_class_edges` - a self-typed or byte view keeps its function tagged, double is a class of its own, and a vector store aliases every class
- `test_the_typed_default_and_the_noalias_hint_both_hoist` - the bound and the addend leave a float-store loop both under the typed model alone and under [hint(noalias = fa)]
- `test_a_hint_naming_no_parameter_is_a_compile_error` - a noalias, nocapture or align16 hint naming no parameter fails the compile with an error naming the hint, the function and its parameters
- `test_a_const_container_parameter_is_not_readonly` - a const array parameter and a const pointer to an array carry no readonly attribute, while a const pointer to a scalar keeps it

### llvm_jit_baseline.das

- `test_baseline_class_replaces_the_box` - under DAS_JIT_BASELINE a kernel-carrying -exe and a -jit run announce the class, never target the box, and bake the class's tier gates on the generic rail
- `test_baseline_refuses_a_foreign_or_unknown_class` - DAS_JIT_BASELINE naming another architecture's class, or a name no class carries, refuses the build and names the reason
- `test_baseline_under_a_cross_target` - under DAS_JIT_BASELINE a cross target of the class's own arch compiles, and one of the other arch is refused against the triple's arch
- `test_exe_host_cpu` - a kernel-carrying -exe targets the build box and bakes the host feature rail, while a kernel-free exe and one that only calls an intrinsic stay on the generic baseline

### llvm_jit_cache.das

- `test_jit_compile_only` - the JIT's compile-only escape emits no partition and reads no cached object, and the program still runs interpreted to the right answer
- `test_jit_obj_cache` - a split JIT build after an edit to one module re-emits every partition and links the two unchanged ones from the object cache
- `test_jit_split_modules` - a split JIT build emits one partition per das module whose cross-partition calls answer right, and a second run hits the same content-addressed DLL without re-emitting
- `test_jit_ast_roundtrip` - a program deserialized from its AST blob hits the DLL its parsed twin wrote, so every function hash survives the serialization round trip
- `test_slot_names_key` - a local turning let moves the JIT DLL key but not the AOT hash, the extern-slot fold ignores the jit selection, and another process folds the same slot names
- `test_layout_term` - a handled layout term changes when the field's offset, the field, the type or the module changes, and a type's size is a term apart from a field's offset
- `test_layout_hash` - the running binary's handled layout hash is the same on every walk and covers handled types that bind no structure
- `test_salt_folds_layouts` - the JIT env salt a compile takes folds this binary's handled layout hash and the typed aliasing switch

### llvm_jit_debug_info.das

- `test_debug_info_is_off_by_default` - a JIT run without --jit-debug emits no compile unit, no variable metadata and no dbg records
- `test_one_compile_unit_per_module` - under --jit-debug the whole module shares one compile unit, tagged DW_LANG_C_plus_plus
- `test_subprograms_carry_the_das_name` - under --jit-debug both halves of a function pair and main carry the das name as their subprogram name, with no linkage name
- `test_locals_and_arguments_are_described` - under --jit-debug every argument and local gets a DILocalVariable and a dbg record, in one lexical block per open das block
- `test_a_global_is_described` - under --jit-debug a das global is described as a variable of each function that touches it, never as a static-address global expression
- `test_types_are_described` - under --jit-debug structs, enums, strings, scalars, dims, containers, refs and vectors reach DWARF as their own type shapes, with scalar encodings and member offsets right
- `test_source_paths_are_absolute` - under --jit-debug the fixture's DIFile names an absolute path and leaves the directory field empty
- `test_hoisted_instructions_carry_no_stale_line` - under --jit-debug the entry block carries no line and declares every argument, and a loop latch reports the loop's own line

### llvm_jit_hints.das

- `test_hint_folds_bind_to_their_function` - the [hint] fold is a function of the source, and the same hint moved to another function changes the key
- `test_an_aliasing_exclusion_rekeys_the_jit_cache` - the strict-aliasing exclusion fold is a function of the source, and the punning view moved to another function changes the key
- `test_never_fast_math_rekeys_the_jit_cache` - [never_fast_math] changes the fold both JIT cache keys take, and moving it to another function changes it again
- `test_never_fast_math_keeps_flags_off` - under options fast_math an unmarked function's multiply is stamped reassoc nsz contract, while a [never_fast_math] function and a block literal in it carry no flag
- `test_never_fast_math_implies_never_inline` - [never_fast_math] sets the function's neverInline flag, so no AST splice moves its arithmetic into an unmarked caller

### llvm_jit_sanitize.das

- `test_jit_sanitize_options` - --jit-sanitize instruments the IR for address, none, the host's own default and address,undefined, and refuses an unknown name and address on the in-memory engine
- `test_asan_runtime` - under --jit-sanitize=address the asan runtime stops every overflow and use-after-delete fixture interpreted and jitted while heap_collect keeps a live object, and a host without the runtime refuses by name

### llvm_tune.das

- `test_llvm_tune` - a [tune] function runs its stamped fallback tier or the reference body and nothing else, its companion follows the same perm, a fallback chain skips an ineligible perm, and no fallback means the reference body
- `test_modes_client_fallback` - a [tune] function with a declined row and fallback k1 runs the k1 tier or the reference body, and its companion follows the same perm
- `test_llvm_tune_grid_mode` - under DAS_TUNE_MODE=test every grid perm runs its own generated body, the reference and declined rows run the reference body, and the companion's grid follows per perm
- `test_llvm_tune_fat` - a fat -exe stamps one clone per profiled CPU class and dispatches by cpuid at startup, DAS_TUNE_FAT_CLASS pins or refuses the pick, and fat mode refuses a non-exe build and a build with no baseline

### llvm_tune_manifest.das

- `test_llvm_tune_manifest_roundtrip` - a child stamps its kernel and companion from the per-app sidecar it wrote, while a binary-stale or other-box sidecar drops back to the fallback unless applied_box names this box
- `test_llvm_tune_sidecar_verdict` - tune_sidecar_verdict names every refusal reason of a sidecar, and the boolean predicate agrees with the verdict on every case
- `test_llvm_tune_stale_save_keeps_runtime` - a save onto this box's binary-stale sidecar keeps only its runtime section, and a save onto another box's stale sidecar keeps nothing

### llvm_tune_progress.das

- `test_non_event_lines_are_not_events` - tuner lines without the @tune prefix are not progress events and start no display
- `test_plan_starts_a_display` - a plan event starts the display with the bar leading the line and a 0/total outer counter
- `test_kernel_counters_and_phase_render` - begin and step events render the kernel name, the pass with its inner counter, and the live-candidate count
- `test_end_advances_the_outer_counter` - each end event advances the outer kernel counter by one

- `test_bar_fills_with_the_outer_counter` - the progress bar is empty at 0 of N kernels and full at N of N
- `test_line_respects_a_narrow_terminal` - on a narrow terminal the bar shrinks to its 8-cell floor and the counters survive

- `test_a_spaced_value_truncates_but_does_not_corrupt` - an event field value containing a space is cut at the space without corrupting the counters

- `test_verbosity_parses_and_defaults` - tune verbosity accepts silent, verbose and normal, and an unknown or empty spelling reads as normal

### llvm_tune_requires.das

- `test_empty_requires_always_passes` - an empty requires= expression passes on every box
- `test_unknown_feature_never_passes` - a requires= naming a feature nothing recognizes never passes
- `test_or_alternatives` - a | in requires= passes exactly when either side's feature is present
- `test_and_conjunction` - a , in requires= fails the whole expression when any one term fails
- `test_plain_chain_is_the_first_entry` - a fallback chain with no gating picks its first entry
- `test_gated_entry_is_skipped_when_it_cannot_pass` - a fallback chain skips every entry whose requires= cannot pass
- `test_chain_with_nothing_eligible_picks_nothing` - a fallback chain with no eligible entry, and an empty chain, pick nothing
- `test_gated_entry_wins_when_its_feature_is_present` - a gated fallback entry wins exactly when this box has its feature
- `test_earlier_entry_wins_over_later` - the earliest eligible entry of a fallback chain wins over every later one

### llvm_tune_scope.das

- `test_llvm_tune_scope_documentation` - a -documentation compile of a tune-scoped app stamps nothing, runs no tune policy and writes no sidecar, even under DAS_TUNE_POLICY=error
- `test_llvm_tune_scope_policy` - the fallback, error, auto and restart policies, a scope resolver, the injected default, --tune, version pins and an unreadable DAS_TUNE_MANIFEST each stamp, tune or refuse as declared across two library scopes sharing one app sidecar
- `test_llvm_tune_profiles` - a shipped defaults profile covers an untuned start with no tuner, races only the families it leaves unlocked, yields to --tune, adopts a lower class's profile, and a relaunched child still reading untuned stops instead of relaunching

### llvm_tune_stats.das

- `test_tune_median` - tune_median takes the middle of an odd sample, the mean of the middle pair of an even one, 0 for none, and leaves its input in order
- `test_tune_cv_pct` - tune_cv_pct is 0 for a flat or single sample and 100 times the sample deviation over the mean otherwise
- `test_tune_noise_env` - the noise threshold ignores its paranoid argument and follows the in-process setters, which mark it overridden
- `test_tune_sidecar_section_merge` - two merges into one sidecar section keep both entries and leave the kernels section untouched
- `test_tune_history_archive` - tune_history_archive copies an ok mint's sidecar into the history dir and writes a refused mint as a FAILED stub carrying its verdict
- `test_tune_provenance_note_roundtrip` - a provenance note lands in the sidecar beside the winner, and a note never overwrites the box identity
- `test_tune_validate_verdict` - the validate verdict passes reproductions, one-window flips and differing challengers, and fails the same challenger past the band in both windows or any rejection

### llvm_vector_math.das

- `test_vector_sin_matches_libm` - the JIT's float4 sin stays within one ulp of libm over |x| up to 1e5
- `test_vector_sin_cos_rail_consistency` - the JIT's sin and cos agree bit for bit with the interpreter at float4, float3 and float2
- `test_vector_cos_matches_libm` - the JIT's float4 cos stays within one ulp of libm over |x| up to 1e5
- `test_vector_sin_narrow_widths` - the JIT's float2 and float3 sin hold the same libm bound as float4
- `test_vector_tan` - the JIT's float4 tan holds its relative-error bands against libm away from poles and agrees bit for bit with the interpreter
- `test_vector_tan_near_poles` - within 1e-3 of a pole the JIT's float4 tan still holds its bound and agrees bit for bit with the interpreter
- `test_vector_exp2` - the JIT's float4 exp2 stays within 4e-7 relative of libm and agrees bit for bit with the interpreter
- `test_vector_log2_and_log` - the JIT's float4 log2 and log hold the estimate's bound against libm across the mantissa and agree bit for bit with the interpreter
- `test_vector_log_special_values` - the JIT's log2 answers -127 for zero, the magnitude's log for a negative, exact powers of two, and the interpreter's value on every special input
- `test_vector_log_narrow_widths` - the JIT's float2 and float3 log2, log and pow agree bit for bit with the interpreter where the polynomial rail applies
- `test_vector_pow` - the JIT's float4 pow stays within 6e-5 relative of libm and agrees bit for bit with the interpreter
- `test_vector_pow_zero_exponent` - the JIT's pow(x, 0) is exactly 1 on every lane and agrees with the interpreter
- `test_vector_pow_negative_base` - the JIT's pow of a negative base flips the sign for an odd exponent, keeps it for an even one, and matches the interpreter lane for lane
- `test_vector_nan_lanes` - a NaN lane stays NaN through tanh, sinh, cosh, tan, sin and cos on both the JIT and the interpreter
- `test_vector_tanh` - the JIT's float4 tanh stays within 8e-7 relative of libm, near zero too, and its divergence from the interpreter's libm stays inside that bound
- `test_vector_sinh_cosh` - the JIT's float4 sinh and cosh stay within 8e-7 relative of libm, and their divergence from the interpreter's libm stays inside that bound
- `test_vector_tanh_saturates` - tanh saturates to within an ulp of +-1 with its sign kept past the clamp edge on every rail, and to exactly +-1 where the emitter runs

### test_tune.das

- `test_variants_match_reference` - [dasllama_tune] emits a plain, u2, vec8 and vec8_u2 clone of a [tune] template, each matching the reference dot exactly

### test_tuned.das

- `test_tuned_reconstitutes` - a [tuned] function pinned to a perm, and one with a fallback perm, both reconstitute the template body and match the reference dot
- `test_tuned_stale_sidecar_perm` - a tune sidecar naming a perm outside the grid stamps the fallback with a stale-mint notice, and the client still compiles and runs
- `test_tuned_sidecar_invalidates_module_cache` - a [tuned] client compiled under -module-cache is served from the cache while its tune sidecar is unchanged and reparsed once the sidecar's content changes
- `test_grid_registry` - [dasllama_grid] emits all seven grid permutations of a template into its variants registry, each callable and within tolerance of the reference dot
- `test_grid_void_registry` - [dasllama_grid] over a void template emits a concrete seven-row registry whose variants run in place

### uncategorized.das

- `test_cache_corruption_selfheal` - a module cache whose first record is corrupted resumes past it, rewrites the stream, and reads clean within two more runs
- `test_class_target_gates` - with_class_target_gates holds the twelve tier gates at the x86-avx2 class's set inside its block and restores every gate after it
- `test_no_llvm_set_is_in_bounds` - no dasLLVM source outside bindings/ calls LLVMSetIsInBounds, whose cast writes the in-bounds flag into a constant-folded GEP through the wrong type
- `test_global_lookup_once_per_function` - JIT code looks each das global up once per function, never inside a loop or ahead of an untaken branch, and a solid-context global takes no lookup at all
- `test_jit_link` - a warm run binds the pinned JIT DLL without loading the emitter, while a cold, stale, disabled-function or other program's DLL is a miss that loads the emitter and emits
- `test_a_pointer_difference_is_arithmetic_not_a_call` - the JIT lowers a pointer difference to inline subtraction instead of a call through the i_das_ptr_diff slot, and a backward distance divides signed
- `test_jit_remarks_print_the_vectorizer_decisions` - --jit-remarks, --jit-remarks-missed and --jit-remarks-analysis each print their vectorizer remarks past a DLL cache hit, and under --jit-debug a remark names the loop's source line
- `test_second_context_literals` - a second context of one program, installing the JIT code the first generated, fills every nested literal at init as the first context did
